review_policy: Conservative mapping for recognizing Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat DLP policy targeting from Security & Compliance PowerShell evidence. Unknown names or structures must not be treated as FAIL.

display_names: Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
notes: Microsoft's New-DlpCompliancePolicy example identifies this GUID as the Microsoft 365 Copilot location and uses Workload=Applications.
Display names are matching aids only; the GUID and workload are stronger evidence than display text.

known_rule_conditions.purpose: Prevent Copilot from processing labeled file/email content.
Restrict Copilot prompt processing when typed prompt text contains selected sensitive information types.
supported_policy_actions: Prevent Copilot from processing content > Processing prompts

known_rule_conditions.purpose: Block external web search grounding when typed prompt text contains selected sensitive information types.
supported_policy_actions: Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches

notes: This marker appears in Microsoft's PowerShell example for blocking Copilot content processing. Actual Get-DlpComplianceRule output must be retained and parsed conservatively.

match_any_display_name: Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat

notes: Used to avoid silently missing changed Microsoft Copilot location metadata. This rule must not produce PASS by itself.

status_rules.PASS: At least one policy/rule pair is readable, targets the known Copilot location GUID or equivalent high-strength marker, and contains expected baseline condition/action coverage.
status_rules.WARN: Copilot policy evidence exists but uses preview scenarios, partial rule coverage, display-name-only/pattern-only matching, manual evidence, unverified distribution, stale mapping, or propagation-delay caveats.
status_rules.FAIL: Only when DLP policy inventory is fully readable, expected policy/rule schema is validated, customer baseline requires Copilot DLP, and no high-strength or manual-review Copilot-targeted policy/rule evidence is present.
status_rules.UNKNOWN: Policy/rule evidence is unreadable, unrecognized, or structurally insufficient without an access/license cause.
status_rules.NOT_ACCESSIBLE: Security & Compliance PowerShell, Purview, or policy read operation returns access/RBAC/consent denial.
status_rules.NOT_LICENSED: Readable entitlement evidence proves required DLP for Copilot capability is absent.

parser_safety_rules: Prefer GUID/workload matches over display-name matches.
Do not classify unrecognized policy locations as FAIL; use UNKNOWN with limitation not_configured_for_assessment or api_unsupported as appropriate.
Retain the raw policy and rule output before normalization.
Record the mapping schema_version and last_reviewed date in every DLP control-check evidence item.
Treat preview DLP subfeatures as WARN unless customer baseline accepts preview controls as sufficient.

If policy output targets workload Applications and contains CopilotExperiences, Copilot, or AI-related action/location markers without the known GUID, classify WARN/manual_review_required rather than ignoring it or emitting FAIL.

Collectors must schema-validate Get-DlpCompliancePolicy/Get-DlpComplianceRule output before interpreting absence. Missing or changed Location/Workload/Rule metadata must produce UNKNOWN with limitation api_unsupported or manual_only, not FAIL.

mapping_completeness.collector_requirement: Collectors must record schema_version and last_reviewed. If stale, classify affected DLP checks as WARN/UNKNOWN with limitation stale_mapping unless the run independently verifies the location metadata.
